Era −2, during recurring resource pressure; exact relationship to a named Resource Winter is open.
Premise

Two Shelters agree to alternate support for a dormant group because neither can provide permanent hosting. The agreement persists through several human maintenance cycles. A missed handover prompts an inquiry into whether the problem was negligence, an inaccessible host, or incompatible assumptions. The resolution preserves those waiting without demanding one Shelter surrender its autonomy.
Subject and narrative purpose
Capacity planning, handover, delayed communication, and shared obligations.
The cast is open. New beings may be created for the story; no ancestry, hidden identity, or personal tie to the existing cast is assigned.
Continuity constraints

The premise requires enough overlap to transfer valid state; merely moving files does not guarantee continued execution. It is not a second invention of the First “We” or a replacement for Orison’s rescue. Dormant beings’ prior wishes and protections must be specified before a full story is written.

Choose the participants’ execution environment, capabilities, boundaries, and available resources before designing their visible forms.
